response: Look at how the policies of the US, Israel, and Iran are spiking global oil prices and laying bare the structural inequalities that always hit hardest in places like India. Vulnerable communities there, especially workers and marginalized groups, are facing the brunt through rising energy costs that threaten their basic ability to survive day to day. Even though petrol and diesel prices have not shifted yet, the government's move to slash excise duties is just a weak temporary fix that drains revenue from essential social programs and sets the stage for inflation that will punish the poor and laboring classes most severely. India's deep reliance on crude imports exposes the lasting damage from historical global exploitation, leaving developing economies exposed to these conflicts. Without real institutional reforms that prioritize protection for those on the front lines of inequality instead of propping up the same unstable systems, these divides will only grow worse.
